rfi.title: Paris suburb shooting suspect 'targeted Muslims, Africans or North Africans'
rfi.description: The man being held over the shootings which took place last Friday in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière – which left one man dead and several people wounded, including an 11-year-old girl – has said he specifically targeted people of Muslim, African or North African appearance, anti-terrorism investigators revealed on Thursday.

rfi.title: Race to find new head of European Central Bank after Lagarde leaves early
rfi.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down in February, months before her term ends, officials said on Thursday, kicking off a race to succeed her against a turbulent backdrop in the eurozone and key elections in France.

rfi.title: Russia-Africa summit tests Moscow's ambitions for broader influence
rfi.description: More than 20 African leaders are in Moscow for a summit that will test Russia's bid to expand its influence on the continent. The two-day Russia-Africa Summit, the third since 2019, comes as Moscow grapples with heavy sanctions over its Ukraine offensive – and as several African governments turn to it for security assistance.

rfi.title: Spain begins three days of national mourning after train crash kills at least 68
rfi.description: Spain on Thursday began three days of official mourning, after a rail collision south of Madrid on Wednesday killed at least 68 people and injured more than 100.

rfi.title: Real Madrid says Mbappé was wrong over Mao Zedong as China fallout continues
rfi.description: Spanish football club Real Madrid, as well as Spanish league bosses, were on Thursday waiting to see if their apologies had led to a thaw in relations with China following striker Kylian Mbappé's comments about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

rfi.title: US judge narrows Macrons' defamation lawsuit against American podcaster
rfi.description: A judge in the United States has ruled that French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte ​could continue their defamation lawsuit against the companies of the American podcaster Candace Owens, but not against Owens herself.

rfi.title: French Senate toughens proposals to make rioters pay for damage
rfi.description: The upper house of the French parliament has toughened a proposed law that would make people who participate in rioting and vandalism liable for up to €10,000, after nationwide protests against failing schools and the cost of living that turned violent in Paris and other cities. Rights groups warn the legislation could undermine the democratic right to protest.

rfi.title: French media protest manhandling of journalists at far-right party rally
rfi.description: More than 40 French media groups, including Radio France International, have called on Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally (RN) to allow them to work freely after journalists were allegedly subjected to rough treatment at a party congress last weekend.

rfi.title: Medical experts warn climate change is now a 'global health emergency'
rfi.description: The damage wreaked by climate change on human health is escalating, experts warn, with deaths from heat, drought and other extreme weather rising faster than the world is taking action to limit global warming. Published on Wednesday, a report by medical journal The Lancet calls for climate change to be declared "a global health emergency".

rfi.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
rfi.description: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival's opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel's pivotal general election.

rfi.title: Egypt's mahrganat music: from the streets to five-star hotels
rfi.description: Born in Egypt’s working-class neighbourhoods, mahraganat music is loud and raw, and these days it is practically impossible to escape. But for the artists behind it, mahraganat is more than just party music: they see it as the latest chapter in Egypt’s rich musical history.

rfi.title: Iraqi court jails seven French nationals over Islamic State membership
rfi.description: An Iraqi court has sentenced seven French nationals to prison for belonging to the Islamic State armed group, handing down the first verdicts in proceedings involving French detainees transferred from Syria last year.

rfi.description: France’s government has promised to replace Parcoursup, the university admissions platform, and to invest in schools and student support, offering a package of concessions aimed at defusing weeks of protests over education and the rising cost of living.

rfi.title: Somalia reports deadly fighting with Al-Shabaab as both sides claim heavy losses

rfi.title: Macron vows to stand firm against disorder during visit to Marseille

euronews.description: More than a dozen EU countries are challenging Brussels' plans to favour electricity over gas, warning that the proposals would undermine national control over energy taxation and grid charges.

euronews.description: Frank S. was sentenced to 12 years in prison, followed by preventive detention. The 69-year-old from Berlin systematically drugged and raped 14 women and filmed the assaults. A further 44 cases are expected to be examined in a separate trial.

euronews.title: Vatican: Century of Mercedes-Benz popemobiles goes on display

euronews.title: Brussels hopes unspent defence loans may help plug Ukraine’s budget hole
euronews.description: The European Commission has reopened €21.3bn in unspent SAFE defence loans, urging EU governments to use them for joint projects with Ukraine, which faces a €70bn budget gap. Brussels cannot force them, but hopes the joint procurement rules will steer some of the money to Kyiv.

lemonde.description: « C’est un dispositif exceptionnel, c’est le même volume que pour le 24 octobre », a expliqué le ministre de l’intérieur, au cours d’un point presse organisé jeudi soir, à deux jours des nouvelles mobilisations sociales.

lemonde.title: Patrick Stewart, acteur britannique célèbre pour ses rôles dans « X-Men » et « Star Trek », est mort
lemonde.description: Bien qu’il soit surtout connu pour ses rôles du professeur Charles Xavier et du capitaine Jean-Luc Picard, respectivement dans « X-Men » et « Star Trek », il a passé la majeure partie de sa carrière sur les planches.

lemonde.title: En Afghanistan, la crise humanitaire s’aggrave sous l’effet de la politique des talibans et faute de financements : « Nous sommes livrés à nous-mêmes »
lemonde.description: Coupes dans l’aide internationale, hausse des prix alimentaires, retours massifs depuis l’Iran et le Pakistan : les crises s’accumulent dans le pays. Les enfants en sont parmi les premières victimes, tandis que les fermetures de centres de santé réduisent les possibilités de les soigner.

lemonde.title: En Ukraine, derrière la mission humanitaire à Olechky, la crainte d’une opération militaire et de propagande russe

lemonde.title: A la BCE, Christine Lagarde annonce son départ et veut « s’engager sur des sujets qui ne sont pas des sujets de politique monétaire »

lemonde.title: Attentat raciste de Trappes : Kevin T., mis en examen pour « assassinat et tentatives d’assassinat terroriste », a reconnu avoir ciblé des personnes « de type musulman » ou « africain »

lemonde.title: Matignon s’apprête à vendre l’hôtel particulier du Haut-Commissariat à la stratégie et au plan
lemonde.description: L’hôtel Beistegui, un petit bijou qui donne sur l’esplanade des Invalides, à Paris, appartient à l’Etat depuis 1971. Sa cession s’inscrit dans un programme visant à récupérer 300 millions d’euros en 2027.

lemonde.description: L’extrait sonore tronqué diffusé à la fin du mois de juin laissait entendre que le chef de file de LFI avait tenu des propos antisémites. L’Arcom a appelé la radio publique à ne pas renouveler un tel « manquement aux exigences d’honnêteté et de rigueur ».

lemonde.title: Au Canada, quinze jeunes poursuivent l’Etat pour inaction climatique, dénonçant une « atteinte injustifiée » à leurs droits

france24fr.description: L'acteur britannique, Patrick Stewart, est mort à l'âge de 86 ans de la maladie d'Alzheimer, selon un communiqué publié jeudi. Il est connu pour avoir joué dans les sagas "X-Men" et "Star Trek".

france24fr.title: Prix du livre Albert-Londres : Arthur Sarradin honore la mémoire des rescapés des prisons syriennes
france24fr.description: Récompensé par le prix Albert-Londres 2026 pour son livre sur la plus cruelle prison du régime de Bachar al-Assad, le journaliste Arthur Sarradin a tenu, avec cet ouvrage, à honorer "la mémoire des survivants de l’univers concentrationnaire syrien". Ce correspondant basé à Beyrouth couvre l'actualité du Proche-Orient en s'efforçant de raconter les vies que la violence politique, les bombes et parfois les médias eux-mêmes, relèguent dans l’ombre.

france24fr.title: Mesures du gouvernement pour les lycéens : Des annonces insuffisantes ?
france24fr.description: Malgré les annonces et la main tendue du gouvernement, les lycéens appellent à continuer la mobilisation espérant plus de concessions de la part de l'exécutif. Marc Perelman en parle avec Louis Létoublon, vice-président de l'organisation "Les Lycéens!", Catherine Tricot, directrice de la revue Regards, Carole Barjon, éditorialiste à la revue Politique et parlementaire et Jean Garrigues, historien.

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : dans les souvenirs de trois anciens olympiens sénégalais
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 À quelques jours des JOJ Dakar 2026, plongez dans les souvenirs de trois anciens olympiens sénégalais. Rencontres avec des légendes comme Serena Williams et Mohamed Ali, moments forts et émotions olympiques… Ils nous racontent leur histoire !

france24fr.title: RD Congo : un centre de soins célèbre la sortie des derniers patients atteints d’Ebola
france24fr.description: Le personnel médical et des habitants d’un centre de traitement dans l’Ituri ont dansé et chanté pour célébrer une première depuis le mois de mai : le centre de soins géré par l’organisation humanitaire Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) ne traite plus aucun patient confirmé d’Ebola.

france24fr.title: Midterms : Barack Obama, le joker des démocrates de la dernière heure
france24fr.description: L’ex-président démocrate Barack Obama a participé en une semaine à trois grands rassemblements de campagne pour les élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis. Au fil des ans, il semble être devenu le joker du camp démocrate dans la dernière ligne droite avant un scrutin. Ce n’est pas un hasard.

france24fr.title: Le sport espagnol rend hommage aux victimes de la collision entre deux trains
france24fr.description: En Espagne, le sport est lui aussi en deuil. Après la collision entre deux trains ce mercredi 28 octobre à Urda, dans le sud de Madrid, de nombreuses équipes et sportifs espagnols ont rendu hommage aux victimes de l'accident.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Israël : accusations de fraude envers le parti arabe, le président appelle au calme
france24fr.description: Le président israélien Isaac Herzog a appelé jeudi 29 octobre à ne pas stigmatiser tout le vote arabe israélien, alors que le camp de Netanyahu et ses alliés accusent les partis de cette minorité de fraudes électorales via des financements étrangers, une enquête a été ouverte.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : une frappe russe tue 13 personnes à la gare centrale de Dnipro
france24fr.description: Une attaque de drone russe a tué treize personnes jeudi 29 octobre à la ​gare ‌centrale de Dnipro, dans l'est ⁠de l'Ukraine, en touchant un quai ‌bondé de voyageurs qui s'apprêtaient à monter ⁠dans un train. Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a exhorté l'Occident à mener des actions "justes et résolues" suite à ces frappes meurtrières.

france24fr.title: Midterms : la Maison Blanche s'apprête-t-elle à conetster les résultats en cas d'echec ?
france24fr.description: À l'approche des midterms qui se dérouleront mardi 3 novembre 2026 aux États-Unis, les sondages indiquent 36 % d'opinion favorable au président ultra conservateur, Donald Trump. En Californie, son ministère de la Justice voulait écarter le butin de 20 000 électeurs dont il contestait la citoyenneté, une demande rejetée par un juge fédéral mercredi 28 octobre. La bataille judiciaire est déjà engagée par l'administration Trump qui tente tout pour remporter ces élections de mi-mandat.

france24fr.title: Accident ferroviaire en Espagne : le roi Felipe XI présent aux chevets des victimes
france24fr.description: Le roi d'Espagne Felipe VI a réclamé jeudi 29 octobre des "mesures" pour éviter une nouvelle catastrophe ferroviaire, au lendemain de la collision de deux trains qui a tué au moins 69 personnes et en a blessé une centaine. Les précisions de Maude Petit-Jové, correspondante France 24 en Espagne.

france24fr.title: Sortie du Tchad de la CPI : une aubaine pour les criminels de guerre soudanais ?
france24fr.description: Les criminels de guerre soudanais réfugiés au Tchad resteront-ils justiciables devant la Cour pénale internationale malgré leur retrait de cette instance en juillet ? Bien que ce retrait ne soit prévu qu'en juillet 2027, il risque d'entraver les investigations sur ces criminels, privant ainsi les victimes, particulièrement celles de viols, de toute perspective de justice.

france24fr.title: Restauration de la nature : l'ONU appelle le monde à accélérer la cadence
france24fr.description: Une restauration sans précédent des écosystèmes est à l’œuvre à travers le monde. Mais elle ne va pas assez vite. C’est ce que montre un rapport de l’ONU publié alors que la COP17 sur la biodiversité, à Erevan, en Arménie, touche à sa fin.

france24fr.title: En France, deux événements d'extrême droite radicale interdits par les autorités
france24fr.description: Deux événements organisés par l'extrême droite radicale ont été interdits jeudi par le préfet des Hauts-de-Seine, ainsi que par la préfecture de Paris une semaine après un attentat raciste dans la région. Les organisateurs ont annoncé déposer un recours devant le tribunal administratif.

france24fr.title: Changement climatique : une “urgence sanitaire mondiale”, alertent des chercheurs
france24fr.description: Le changement climatique est une “urgence sanitaire mondiale”, affirment 146 chercheurs du Lancet Countdown dans un rapport publié le 28 octobre 2026 par la revue médicale The Lancet. Entre 2016 et 2023, la chaleur liée au réchauffement aurait “causé près de 3 millions de décès”. Cette alerte intervient à quelques jours de la COP31, prévue du 9 au 20 novembre en Turquie.

france24fr.title: Tchad : le pays dément les accusations du Niger concernant une frappe de drone
france24fr.description: Le Niger estime que son voisin, le Tchad, est responsable de la mort de deux civils sur son territoire, suite à une frappe de drone survenue le 24 octobre dernier. Le Tchad dément lui tout implication. La junte accuse également la France d'être impliquée. Les précisions de Harold Girard, correspondant France 24 à Njdaména.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : Obama se moque de Trump à l'approche des midterms
france24fr.description: À cinq jours des les élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis, Barack Obama s’est rendu en Géorgie pour apporter son soutien au sénateur sortant Jon Ossoff. L'ancien président a commenté une ​plaisanterie qu’il avait faite la veille. "Il était très contrarié par mes remarques sur la Cheesecake Factory", a-t-il assuré. "Ils ont mobilisé l’ensemble de l’appareil d’État pour réagir à cette blague. Pas à l’inflation, mais à cette blague." À l'approche du scrutin, les sondages laissent entrevoir une pos

france24fr.title: Les excuses de Kylian Mbappé envers la Chine suffiront-elles à limiter les pertes économiques ?
france24fr.description: Si Kylian Mbappé, le Real Madrid et la Liga ont rapidement présenté leurs excuses pour les propos de l'attaquant vedette sur Mao Zedong, les dommages causés à leur réputation en Chine ne seront ni faciles ni rapides à réparer. Et le football espagnol a beaucoup à perdre au vu des relations commerciales qu'il entretient avec cette puissance économique.

zeit.description: Er war vor allem als Captain Picard in der Serie »Star Trek« und als Professor in den »X-Men«-Filmen bekannt. Patrick Stewart ist im Alter von 86 Jahren gestorben.

Todesfall: Captain Picard und Theaterveteran: Patrick Stewart ist tot
Alexander Zverev: Alexander Zverev übernimmt Platz eins der Tennisweltrangliste
zeit.description: Beim ATP-Turnier in Wien besiegt Alexander Zverev den Niederländer Tallon Griekspoor. Ab Montag ist der 29-Jährige damit die Nummer eins der Tennisweltrangliste.

zeit.title: Die Linke Berlin: Ist Rot-Grün-Rot jetzt vom Tisch? So einfach ist es nicht
zeit.description: Mit ihrer Angst vor einem Terrorsympathisanten gefährdet Elif Eralp die Berliner Koalitionsverhandlungen. Doch SPD und Grüne stützen die Linken-Politikerin. Ein bisschen

zeit.title: Alexander Zverev: Sein langer Weg zur Nummer 1
zeit.description: 2026 ist das Jahr von Alexander Zverev. Wie er seine Zweifel besiegte und zur Nummer eins wurde – und warum dies nicht nur am Verletzungspech seiner Konkurrenten lag.

zeit.title: Charlotte Bartels: »Die hohen Mieten sind das Schlüsselproblem der Gen Z«
zeit.description: Wer über den Frust junger Leute spricht, muss auch über Erbschaften und Immobilienpreise sprechen, sagt die Ökonomin Charlotte Bartels. Vermögen aufzubauen sei schwierig.

zeit.title: Obdachlosigkeit in Hamburg: »So kann es nicht weitergehen«
zeit.description: 27 Obdachlose sind im letzten Winter in Hamburg gestorben. Nun öffnet die Stadt wieder ihre Notunterkünfte – doch das reicht nicht, sagt der Leiter der Stadtmission.

zeit.title: UN-Generalsekretär: Orbáns Chancen stehen schlecht. Aber vielleicht wird’s diese Frau?
zeit.description: In diesen Tagen entscheidet sich, wer UN-Generalsekretär wird. Beste Chancen scheint eine Überraschungskandidatin vom Golf zu haben. Aber die wird auch massiv kritisiert.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Russland greift Kiew erneut mit ballistischen Raketen an
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Novak Djokovic scheidet an den Swiss Indoors in der zweiten Runde aus
nzz.description: Der Serbe scheitert in Basel erstmals bereits vor den Halbfinals. Er unterliegt gegen den Deutschen Jan-Lennard Struff in drei Sätzen.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN KULTUR - Britischer Schauspieler Patrick Stewart ist gestorben
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Feuilleton.

nzz.title: Alexander Zverev wird die Nummer eins – und Boris Becker ist wieder sein grösster Fan
nzz.description: Die deutsche Tennislegende begleitet Zverev seit je sehr eng. Er ist Förderer und scharfer Kritiker zugleich. Mit den jüngsten Erfolgen des 29-Jährigen wandelt sich ihr ambivalentes Verhältnis einmal mehr.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Wahlen in Israel: Nach Auszählung aller Stimmen liegt das Lager von Netanyahu zwar vorn, verfehlt aber eine Mehrheit
nzz.description: Israel wählt ein neues Parlament. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Schuldenkrise, Weltbühne, Geldpolitik: Christine Lagardes prägende Momente
nzz.description: Die erste Frau an der Spitze von IWF und EZB: Christine Lagarde prägte über zwei Jahrzehnte die internationale Wirtschaftspolitik. Ein Rückblick in Bildern.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: Hegseth feuert nächsten Spitzenfunktionär
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Eine Politikerin, die sich von Extremisten bedroht fühlt, kann nicht die Sicherheit in der deutschen Hauptstadt verantworten
nzz.description: Linken-Spitzenkandidatin Elif Eralp will Berlins Regierende Bürgermeisterin werden. Ihre Angst vor einem Milieu mit Hamas-Kontakten wirft Zweifel an ihrer Eignung auf, ob sie den Schutz der Bürger in Berlin gewährleisten kann.

nzz.title: Wie konnte es erneut zu einem tödlichen Zugunglück in Spanien kommen? Eine visuelle Rekonstruktion
nzz.description: Innert 17 Minuten passierten die Fehler, die zum verheerenden Aufprall von zwei Schnellzügen führten. Aufgezeichnete Funkgespräche deuten auf technisches und menschliches Versagen hin.

nzz.title: «Ein Betrug wie aus dem Lehrbuch»: langjährige Gefängnisstrafe für Ex-SBB-Kadermann
nzz.description: Als führender Mitarbeiter des SBB-Werks Olten veruntreute der Beschuldigte mit fiktiven Rechnungen mehrere Millionen Franken – für ein Leben in Saus und Braus.

nzz.title: Cassis in Nordkorea: Die Schweiz sucht den Draht zum Kim-Regime
nzz.description: 23 Jahre nach Micheline Calmy-Reys historischem Grenzübertritt in Nordkorea reist mit Ignazio Cassis wieder ein amtierender Bundesrat in die abgeschottete Diktatur. Die Mission berührt Fragen der Guten Dienste und der Neutralität – inmitten einer sich verändernden Weltordnung.

nzz.title: Immobilienmarkt: Die Städte exportieren ihre Probleme aufs Land und in andere Kantone
nzz.description: Ein scheinbares Paradox prägt den Wohnungsmarkt: Dieses und vor allem nächstes Jahr wird deutlich mehr gebaut. Trotzdem steigen die Immobilienpreise ungebremst weiter. Bei den Mieten flacht der Anstieg höchstens leicht ab.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Karikatur der Woche
nzz.description: Der Karikaturist Peter Gut kommentiert in seinen wöchentlichen Zeichnungen für die NZZ das Weltgeschehen.

nzz.title: Die Fahrt muss weitergehen – aber in Spanien steigen selbst Mitarbeiter nur noch mit mulmigem Gefühl in den Zug
nzz.description: Das Land trauert um die mindestens 69 Toten des zweiten schweren Unglücks in einem Jahr. Die Fehler im System werden immer offenkundiger.

nzz.title: Bolsonaros Flucht in die USA könnte ausgerechnet Präsident Lula stärken
nzz.description: Von Miami aus will der Wahlverlierer die brasilianische Opposition anführen. Doch selbst seine engsten Verbündeten gehen auf Distanz. Neue Enthüllungen über dubiose Finanzgeschäfte könnten den gesamten Bolsonaro-Clan in Bedrängnis bringen.

spiegel.title: Russland-Ukraine-Krieg: Russland greift Kyjiw mit Raketen an
spiegel.description: Wieder greift das russische Militär die ukrainische Hauptstadt Kyjiw mit ballistischen Raketen an. Explosionen sind zu hören. Zuvor hatte der ukrainische Präsident seine Verbündeten um mehr Waffen zur Luftverteidigung gebeten.

spiegel.title: Patrick Stewart: Fans und Wegbegleiter trauern um Captain Jean-Luc Picard
spiegel.description: Patrick Stewart hat als Schauspieler Millionen fasziniert und berührt: Jetzt trauern Kollegen und Politiker um den britischen Schauspieler. Der schönste Satz über ihn stammt von Hikaru Sulu, einem Steuermann der »Enterprise«.

spiegel.title: Eralp führt Angst-Eingeständnis auf Rat von Sicherheitsbehörden zurück
spiegel.description: Elif Eralp nimmt Stellung zu ihrer vom SPIEGEL enthüllten Furcht vor Terrorsympathisanten. Auf Instagram berichtet die Berliner Linkenpolitikerin davon, dass sie seit der Wahl vermehrt Bedrohungen erhalte.

spiegel.title: Uni Leipzig nach Hackerangriff weiter offline
spiegel.description: Der Betrieb an der Universität Leipzig bleibt nach einem Hackerangriff beeinträchtigt. Zur Schadensabwehr hatte die Hochschule alle Server vom Netz genommen.

spiegel.title: Brasilien: Flávio Bolsonaro stößt nach Ausreise auf Kritik im eigenen Lager
spiegel.description: Nach seiner heimlichen Ausreise in die USA stellt Brasiliens Wahlverlierer Flávio Bolsonaro das Wahlergebnis infrage. Selbst Verbündete weisen seine Betrugsvorwürfe zurück.

spiegel.title: »Lake Ontario« vs. »Lake America« – Bryan Adams singt gegen Trump
spiegel.description: Der kanadische Musiker Bryan Adams äußert sich häufig zu politischen Themen. Jetzt hat er einen Protestsong gegen Trump veröffentlicht – auch die Epstein-Dokumente kommen vor.

spiegel.title: Jeffrey Epstein: Wie Assistentinnen neue Opfer suchten - Podcast Firewall
spiegel.description: Das Versprechen auf ein Model-Casting führt sie zu Jeffrey Epstein. Erst missbraucht er die junge Russin, dann soll sie neue Frauen anwerben. Der Podcast »Firewall« rekonstruiert, wie ein Opfer zur Komplizin wurde.

spiegel.title: Kai Maaz über Proteste der Gen Z: »Bildungspolitik gehört jetzt symbolisch ins Kanzleramt«
spiegel.description: Am Samstag wollen deutschlandweit junge Menschen unter dem Motto »Gen Z regelt« auf die Straße gehen. Der Bildungsforscher Kai Maaz sagt, warum die Proteste berechtigt sind und wo es an Schulen am meisten hakt.

spiegel.title: Patrick Stewart ist tot
spiegel.description: Er war Captain Jean-Luc Picard in »Star Trek« und Professor Charles Francis Xavier in »X-Men«. Jetzt ist der britische Schauspieler und Filmproduzent Sir Patrick Stewart nach kurzer schwerer Krankheit im Alter von 86 Jahren gestorben.

spiegel.title: EU und Kanada: Friedrich Merz durchkreuzt Kanada-Plan von Ursula von der Leyen
spiegel.description: Kommissionschefin von der Leyen hätte Kanada gern als »assoziiertes Mitglied« der EU gesehen. Doch ihr Vorstoß kam in der Bundesregierung nicht gut an, Kanzler Merz ging dazwischen.

spiegel.title: USA: Demokraten wollen Regierungsfragen an KI-Chatbots aufbewahren
spiegel.description: Abgeordnete der Demokraten fordern, dass Fragen der US-Regierung an KI-Chatbots und deren Antworten aufbewahrt werden. Sie werfen die Frage auf, ob KI politische Entscheidungen der US-Regierung beeinflusst hat.

spiegel.title: AfD Niedersachsen scheitert mit Beschwerde gegen vorläufige Hochstufung vom Verfassungsschutz
spiegel.description: Der Verfassungsschutz durfte die AfD Niedersachsen zum Beobachtungsobjekt von erheblicher Bedeutung hochstufen. Das Oberverwaltungsgericht Lüneburg hat eine entsprechende Entscheidung des Verwaltungsgerichts Hannover bestätigt.

spiegel.title: Alexander Zverev steht ab Montag auf Platz eins der Tennis-Weltrangliste
spiegel.description: Durch einen Achtelfinalerfolg gegen den Niederländer Tallon Griekspoor in Wien hat Alexander Zverev einen Meilenstein seiner Karriere erreicht: Ab nächster Woche führt er die Tennis-Weltrangliste an.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Täter bekennt sich zu rassistischem Motiv nach Anschlag bei Paris
spiegel.description: Bei dem Anschlag in zwei Pariser Vorstädten wurde der 26-jährige Pengo Bossio Wangi umgebracht, fünf weitere Menschen wurden verletzt. Der Täter gab nun zu: Er handelte aus rassistischer Überzeugung.

spiegel.title: Dortmund: Auto-Influencer JP Kraemer muss 270.000 Euro zahlen
spiegel.description: Er soll seine Nochehefrau geschlagen und misshandelt haben, nun muss der Tuningexperte sich wegen Körperverletzung in zwei Fällen und Sachbeschädigung verantworten. Das Amtsgericht Dortmund hat einen Strafbefehl erlassen.

spiegel.title: Stinkwanzen: Wie problematisch sind sie und wie wird man sie los?
spiegel.description: Im Herbst suchen Stinkwanzen gern Unterschlupf in Wohnungen. Ein Experte erklärt, was man gegen die Insekten tun kann und warum sie besser sind als ihr Ruf.

spiegel.title: Kambodscha: Passagiere der »Odyssey« nach Abbruch der Weltreise obdachlos
spiegel.description: Das Kreuzfahrtschiff »Odyssey« hat seine dreijährige Weltreise vorzeitig in Kambodscha gestoppt, Grund seien zu hohe Treibstoffkosten. Einige Passagiere sind jetzt obdachlos. Warum? Und wie geht es jetzt weiter?

spiegel.title: Berlin: Denkmalschützer wollen eine Nazi-Bunkeranlage erhalten – warum?
spiegel.description: In Berlin wird heftig über die Zukunft einer Bunkeranlage unter der früheren Neuen Reichskanzlei gestritten. Experten plädieren dafür, die Überreste unter Denkmalschutz zu stellen.

observador.title: Queda de helicóptero militar na Bósnia faz quatro mortos
observador.description: Helicóptero estaria a voar em baixa altitude e começou a rodar sobre si próprio antes de se despenhar. As causas do acidente permanecem desconhecidas.

observador.title: As notícias das 21h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Famalicão na final four da Taça da Liga pela primeira vez
observador.description: Gabriel Cabral defendeu três penáltis e foi decisivo. Em Leiria, entre 5 e 9 de janeiro, o Famalicão defronta o Sporting nas meias-finais.

observador.title: Castro Almeida: Portugal ainda é beneficiário líquido da UE
observador.description: Saldo positivo de 3.100 milhões. Castro Almeida confirmou, na Assembleia da República, que 75% do benefício vem do Portugal 2030 e o restante do PEPAC.

observador.title: Corina Machado assegura que transição irreversível
observador.description: A líder da oposição avisa que o caminho para a democracia está a avançar e que, no processo "para a liberdade, os venezuelanos tornaram-se muito melhores", agora que regressou pode "sanar o país".

observador.title: Porto. BE diz que câmara confirmou articuluzação com PSP
observador.description: Município liderado por Pedro Duarte deixou por esclarecer quem decidiu as operações e que instruções foram dadas. Bens apreendidos só devolvidos após pagamento de coima.

observador.title: Ex-ministra e atleta entre os mortos do acidente de comboios
observador.description: Fátima Báñez, ex-ministra do Trabalho de Rajoy, e a atleta Julieta Gallego estão entre as vítimas da colisão de comboios que aconteceu esta quarta-feira. Rangel confirma um português desaparecido.

observador.title: Açores. Ordem dos Médicos preocupada com listas da espera
observador.description: Com 13.945 doentes em espera cirúrgica — recorde desde 2017 — Carlos Cortes exige resposta mais rápida e mais médicos, blocos e camas no hospital de Ponta Delgada.

observador.title: Quatro portugueses presos por motivos políticos na Venezuela
observador.description: O ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros revelou que três portugueses estão em prisão efetiva e um em prisão domiciliária, apesar das acusações de delitos comuns.

observador.title: Ventura admite que não daria asilo a Flávio Bolsonaro
observador.description: Líder do Chega separou o "André", próximo da família Bolsonaro, do "titular político português" e disse que não teria condições de dar asilo a Flávio se a situação se colocasse.

observador.title: Portugal redefine prioridades do Fundo de Modernização da UE
observador.description: O Ministério do Ambiente e Energia adianta que a agência deverá identificar as áreas prioritárias para a apresentação de candidaturas ao Comité de Investimento do Fundo de Modernização em 2027.

observador.title: Lisboa. Centenas de polícias protestam por melhores salários
observador.description: Centenas de polícias e guardas concentraram-se no Largo de Camões para exigir salários mais altos e cumprimento do acordo assinado com o Governo em 2024.

observador.title: Portugal entre 12 países que vão libertar barris de petróleo
observador.description: Portugal é um dos 12 países que vão disponibilizar 42,6 milhões de barris até janeiro de 2027. Decisão segue apelo do G7 e da Agência Internacional de Energia.

observador.title: CGTP convoca "grande manifestação" para 21 de novembro
observador.description: A central sindical anunciou ainda uma concentração em frente à Assembleia da República a 24 de novembro, dia da votação final global do Orçamento do Estado para 2027.

observador.title: “Assis está claramente errado”
observador.description: Luís Testa, vice-presidente da bancada parlamentar do PS, diz que o eurodeputado socialista não tem razão quando critica os deputados do partido que se juntaram às manifestações.

observador.title: Habitação. Olhão aprova investimento de 40 milhões de euros
observador.description: O município de Olhão aprovou um empréstimo de 49 milhões de euros, dos quais 40 milhões para habitação, numa resposta à crise que afeta em particular o Algarve.

observador.title: BdP. PS pede explicações sobre nova sede
observador.description: Deputado Carlos Pereira diz que nova solução — uma só torre por 225 milhões — "custa mais por metro quadrado" e exige explicações ao governador há três meses em falta.

observador.title: 828 menores vivem há pelo seis anos em casas de acolhimento
observador.description: O relatório CASA 2025 mostra que os acolhimentos prolongados resistem: 17% das crianças em casas generalistas ficam no sistema por seis ou mais anos.

phys-org.title: Chemical recycling turns silicone waste into reusable building blocks with up to 99% yield

However, it is precisely these properties that have made recycling silicones extremely problematic in the past. Researchers at the Institute of Chemistry at TU Berlin have now succeeded in breaking down the polymer chains of silicone molecules into their basic building blocks. The resulting molecule dimethyldichlorosilane can then be reused as a starting material for the

phys-org.title: Borneo's wildfires could have a lasting impact on orangutans
phys-org.description: Indonesia is battling one of its most severe wildfire seasons in over a decade, as intense El Niño conditions fuel widespread drought. Some of the most severely affected areas are on the island of Borneo. Peatlands across West, Central and South Kalimantan are smoldering underground, releasing smoke haze that threatens human health and the environment.

phys-org.title: Qinghai–Tibet Plateau study traces evolution of terrestrial animals across three distinct regions
phys-org.description: A new study has pieced together the evolutionary history of terrestrial animals on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP), offering a comprehensive picture of how the distinctive fauna of the "Third Pole" took shape over millions of years.

phys-org.title: The human surfaceome: AI flags potential cell surface drug targets overlooked by major databases
phys-org.description: More than 65% of approved medicines work by binding to proteins on the surface of human cells. Yet scientists developing new treatments face a fundamental problem: Major biological databases disagree about which proteins are actually found on cell surfaces.

phys-org.title: The 'shape' of gene expression: Identifying genes that may share roles across species
phys-org.description: Much of what we know about biology comes from animal models, particularly mice. Applying these insights to humans, however, is not always straightforward. For example, some of the genes important for the formation of germ cells, which eventually give rise to eggs or sperm, differ between mice and humans.

phys-org.title: Nature finance needs a fundamental rethink, researchers argue
phys-org.description: The authors call on governments, investors and conservation organizers to reimagine nature finance based on a central tenet: raising funds should be a means to an end, not an end in itself.

phys-org.title: How the quantum vacuum perturbs atoms, could shrink black holes and may have helped form galaxies
phys-org.description: The word "vacuum" may conjure the image of empty space. Maybe you think of a region far outside the solar system without planets, debris, gas clouds or light. According to quantum theory, however, a vacuum is never truly empty. Quantum mechanics extends the Heisenberg uncertainty principle—which states that we cannot measure the position and the velocity of an object exactly at the same time—to a vacuum. The result is that a vacuum can never be still.

phys-org.title: Detailed images reveal ribosome assembly inside human cells for the first time
phys-org.description: For decades, ribosomes have been under the lens of many scientists. Ribosomes are highly sophisticated and complex molecular machines that allow cells to synthesize proteins. However, putting ribosomes together requires intricate assembly processes. While many underlying mechanisms for building ribosomes have been discovered ex situ (outside their native cellular context), our understanding of how ribosomes are assembled in situ has so far remained limited.

phys-org.title: Eyewitnesses remember feedback better after making an identification, study finds
phys-org.description: An eyewitness can tell the truth, believe every word they say and still send an innocent person to prison. A new study by Stephen Charman from FIU's Department of Psychology takes on a question that has challenged the justice system for decades: Can we rely on eyewitnesses to help identify the person responsible for a crime?

phys-org.title: Terahertz light distinguishes two groups of particles trapped inside superconducting vortices
phys-org.description: Scientists at Rutgers and in Estonia have used invisible light to look into tiny magnetic whirlpools, called vortices, inside a superconductor, revealing details that could help researchers develop better materials for carrying electricity.

phys-org.title: What animal bones in Malawi teach us about the social lives of people long ago
phys-org.description: In the ancient past, when human communities were small and the only way to travel was by walking, what were the chances of meeting a stranger? And what would happen next?

phys-org.title: European rivers retain far more plastic than they carry to the sea, study finds
phys-org.description: Plastic that enters the environment does not necessarily make its way to the sea via rivers. In fact, only a tiny fraction eventually reaches river mouths. Most plastic remains on land or within river systems.

phys-org.title: Wild orchids face growing challenges as conservation falls short
phys-org.description: At first glance, it is easy to see why Corybas puniceus has captured the attention of collectors around the world. Small enough to fit in the palm of your hand, its unusual shape and bursts of color make it unlike almost anything else in the orchid world. The species, found only in Southeast Asia, is classified as critically endangered.

phys-org.title: How eggs protect chromosome connections during prolonged dormancy
phys-org.description: Eggs follow a very different developmental path from sperm. Once a male hits puberty, sperm cells are produced continuously throughout his life. Eggs, however, are all produced during the fetal stage. Once formed, eggs enter a long dormant state called the dictyate stage, in which the process of cell division (meiosis) is paused partway through. This dormant period ends only when the egg is ovulated.

phys-org.title: Sealing gaps and securing food can fight rodent infestations while protecting predators
phys-org.description: Mice and rats can spread dangerous viruses and bacteria, trigger asthma attacks and damage property with their constant gnawing. So when rodents get indoors, most people take action to help keep their home safe.

phys-org.title: Machine learning helps track semiconductor defects under more realistic temperature conditions
phys-org.description: All materials contain inherent defects. These are not always harmful, since they can be used to engineer and introduce certain properties into a material. However, it is crucial to understand how they function and how they affect the material's properties.

phys-org.title: Machine-learning models predict human health from microbiome data
phys-org.description: Inside the gut, on the surface of the skin and lining your ears, mouth and nose are colonies of millions of microbes. For every human cell you have, there are at least as many microbial cells associated with your body.

phys-org.title: What drives temperature preferences? Female mice have temperature sensors tuned to run warmer
phys-org.description: Female mice like warmer spaces than males because of two types of tiny temperature sensors in their nerves which are tuned to switch on at higher temperatures, according to researchers at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience (IoPPN) at King's College London. The study, led by researchers at the Wolfson Sensory, Pain and Regeneration Centre at IoPPN and published in The Journal of Physiology, explains at a molecular level a sex difference seen in every mammal studied so far

undark.title: The FDA Wants to Pull Its Approval of a Drug. It’s Not So Easy.
undark.description: In 2021, the FDA was on the fence about whether to approve a new treatment for a rare form of vasculitis. After an advisory committee narrowly recommended approval, the agency greenlit the drug, Tavneos, and it started making its way into clinics. After uncovering evidence of what it says is data manipulation in the original trial, the agency wants to rescind the approval. But it’s not so easy.

undark.title: Podcast: The Entanglements Series Finale
undark.description: Welcome to the last installment of Entanglements, at least for the foreseeable future. In this final episode, hosts Brooke Borel and Anna Rothschild are joined by Undark editor-in-chief Tom Zeller Jr. to talk about the show’s successes, failures, and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Michael Geruso, an associate professor of economics at the University of Texas at Austin, and Jennifer Dowd, a professor of demography and population health at the University of Oxford, about population trends and fertility rates.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

proj-syn.title: The New Geopolitics of Mining
proj-syn.description: While the US and China want their critical-mineral investments to deliver the biggest returns possible, governments in resource-rich countries must balance external pressures with internal demands. Mining firms must also win local communities’ trust, as host countries will be quick to throw them under the bus if public opinion sours.

proj-syn.title: Can Bond Vigilantes Prevent the Next Debt Crisis?
proj-syn.description: With interest rates on government debt having gone from near zero to much higher levels in recent years, rising short- and long-term bond yields have cast doubt on the sustainability of some debts and led many to wonder if a crisis might be looming. While some countries are more protected than others, none is immune.

proj-syn.title: A Wealth Tax Would Harm California
proj-syn.description: Before approving a one-time tax on the wealth of billionaires who lived in the state at a certain point in time, Californians should consider what such a policy will do to future tax revenues. Since wealth is mobile, those who stand to lose the most will simply leave, taking their future income-tax payments with them.

proj-syn.title: A Future for Europe’s Youth
proj-syn.description: The current generation of young Europeans possesses freedoms, material resources, opportunities to travel, and technological capabilities beyond anything previous generations could have imagined. Their demands, however, are strikingly simple: decent schools, secure jobs, affordable homes, and the possibility of raising a family.

proj-syn.title: A Tale of Two Chinas
proj-syn.description: China’s economy is deeply unbalanced, with a battered real-estate sector, weak consumption, and stark regional disparities coexisting with dynamic tech and export sectors. But provided that political stability is maintained, China could continue to be a global powerhouse even as hundreds of millions of its citizens remain poor.

proj-syn.title: Sino–American Stability?
proj-syn.description: Delegates at the Bund Summit in Shanghai largely agreed that the US-China relationship could be entering a new, less contentious chapter, although many were more interested in what the post-Trump era will mean for Sino-American ties. But perhaps the most heartening sign for the future was the honest exchange of views.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Winter of Discontent
proj-syn.description: Although it is true that European integration has always been forged through crisis, the continent’s postwar story was largely one of incremental responses to relatively manageable challenges. Today, the European Union is facing multiple, interrelated problems that challenge its very raison d’être.

proj-syn.title: How Students Dethroned Serbia’s Strongman
proj-syn.description: Following the ouster of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power earlier this year, the world has once again witnessed the merits of “old-school” campaigning. In toppling their own country's strongman, Serbia's new student-led opposition offers important lessons for those defending democracy elsewhere.

proj-syn.title: What a US-China AI Safety Channel Needs
proj-syn.description: Addressing AI safety risks depends on close collaboration between the two leading AI powers, and the establishment of an incident-reporting channel is just a small step in this direction. But success will require that the US and Chinese governments actually understand what is happening under their own noses.

proj-syn.title: The Authoritarian Logic of Selective Privacy
proj-syn.description: Around the world, governments are increasingly deciding who gets privacy and who is denied it, a double standard that turns a fundamental democratic right into a privilege. US President Donald Trump’s administration is a prime example, shielding ICE agents from scrutiny while expanding surveillance of immigrants and protesters.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Chapter in the Anti-Authoritarian Playbook
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s renewed democratic confidence must now be matched by institutional and structural reforms and a willingness to build coalitions beyond the left. Recent democratic outcomes in Hungary and Serbia offer useful lessons.

proj-syn.title: Another Crash Landing for Brazil’s Economy?
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s floating exchange rate, high foreign-exchange reserves, strong commodity exports, and debt denominated predominantly in its own currency reduce its exposure to a balance-of-payments crisis. Nonetheless, continued fiscal deterioration under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will carry high domestic costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Make-or-Break Moment Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has not only abandoned Ukraine and America’s European allies, but has increasingly sided with Russian President Vladimir Putin. To preserve their sovereignty, Europeans must remain united in the face of outside pressure, which in turn requires managing political threats from within their borders.

proj-syn.title: Middle Powers Can Lead on AI Safety
proj-syn.description: With the United States showing no interest in regulating AI, middle powers have an opportunity to take the lead on governance. By banding together, these countries could condition market access on meeting a common set of safety requirements and explore joint investment in technical capacity.

proj-syn.title: Lula Killed the Donroe Doctrine
proj-syn.description: In attempting to disentangle the United States from the rest of the world and retreat into a seemingly controllable hemispheric stronghold, Donald Trump's Latin America strategy had fared better than the rest of his foreign policy. But following a defeat for the far right in Brazil, his project now looks dead in the water.

proj-syn.title: The Wrong Way to Compare Economic Size
proj-syn.description: At the European Central Bank’s annual research conference, Paul Krugman concluded that, when it comes to “weaponized interdependence,” the EU is more powerful than both the US and China. But his reliance on PPP-adjusted GDP as a way to smooth out the volatility of nominal exchange rates ignores the even greater swings in PPP data.

proj-syn.title: Public Control for a Purposeful Economy
proj-syn.description: As more governments recognize the need for greater public control over economic outcomes, they must be careful to define the concept well. What ultimately matters is not ownership, but the state’s capacity to steer economic activity toward strategic objectives in the service of the common good.

proj-syn.title: Rethinking Sustainable Livelihoods From the Ground Up
proj-syn.description: In regions where economic activity has long revolved around fossil-fuel extraction, ensuring a just transition requires developing alternative livelihoods that account for each community’s specific needs. Regional endowment funds could be a useful vehicle for funding these local initiatives.
